newsitem.title: ITALY: Castro hopes U.S. will ease Cuba blockade.
newsitem.headline: Castro hopes U.S. will ease Cuba blockade.

text.p: Cuban President Fidel Castro, describing the U.S. economic blockade of his country as "attempted genocide" said on Sunday he hoped President Bill Clinton would move to ease it following his re-election.

Castro told a news conference at the World Food Summit that he hoped a reference in the conference declaration, approved by the United States, that food should not be used as an economic or political weapon would lead to a change from Washington.
"Now that the election campaign is over in the United States of America, I think President Clinton and his administration...will be able to do something to follow this agreement," Castro said.
But he said it would be difficult because of opposition in the Republican-dominated U.S. Congress to any easing of the blockade that has lasted for 34 years.
The veteran communist leader described U.S. policy towards Cuba as "attempted genocide against our country".
"I think this is a crime against humankind," he said.
